name: South Dakota

agency.name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

overview: South Dakota GFP issues limited big game and turkey licenses through season-by-season online lottery drawings, with first, second and later draws followed by first-come leftover sales. Unsuccessful first-choice applicants earn (elk, sheep, goat) or may buy ($5 resident, $20 nonresident) one preference point per season per year, and GFP cubes the number of entries an applicant receives before each draw. Licenses are allocated through ordered pools - landowner, then preference-point tiers (e.g. 2+, 1+, 0+ for deer, antelope and turkey; 10+, 2+, 0+ for elk), then second choices. Elk, bighorn sheep and mountain lion are resident-only.

species.drawSystemSummary: Only South Dakota residents may apply for elk, and a person may hold one elk license per year; seasons are drawn in order (CSP Firearms, CSP Early Archery, Black Hills Firearms, Prairie Firearms, Black Hills Archery, CSP Special Antlerless). For Black Hills firearms, archery and prairie drawings 50% of a unit's licenses go to approved landowners, then 30% to a 10+ preference pool, 15% to a 2+ pool and 5% to a 0+ pool (Custer State Park: 34% 15+, 33% 10+, 33% 0+); GFP cubes the number of entries per applicant, so points improve but do not guarantee odds.
species.residentNote: Unsuccessful first-choice elk applicants receive one preference point per season automatically. Successful applicants who used points lose them and cannot apply in the first draw for that season (or buy points for it) for nine years; CSP Early Archery and CSP Firearms elk are once in a lifetime. There are no second choices in the first elk draw; maximum group size is 2; a $10 non-refundable application fee is charged per season.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents are not eligible to apply for or receive a South Dakota elk license.
species.otcSummary: No over-the-counter elk license. GFP's 2026 elk application lists Unlimited any-elk (type 21) licenses for Prairie unit PRE-ERA, and a Prairie Elk landowner-own-land license is applied for separately (2026: Jul 14 - Dec 31).

species.drawSystemSummary: Deer licenses are drawn season by season (West River, East River, Black Hills, Custer State Park, Muzzleloader, National Wildlife Refuge, Special Buck and others) in a combined deer draw that limits how many applications a person may submit. In the first draw, 50% of a unit's licenses are offered to qualifying landowners with preference, then a 2+ preference pool receives 50% plus any landowner leftovers, then 1+ and 0+ pools (no 0+ applicant draws until every 1+ applicant has a license), then second choices; within each pool GFP cubes the number of times an applicant's name is entered, which improves but does not guarantee odds.
species.residentNote: Residents are eligible for all units with some exceptions. Unsuccessful first-choice applicants may buy one preference point per season per year ($5 resident); points must be used for the first choice in the first draw and are lost when a license is drawn with them. Residents who held a Custer State Park buck license in the preceding nine years may not apply for CSP deer.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents may apply for West River, Black Hills, Muzzleloader (antlerless whitetail only), Refuge and West River Special Buck deer; East River deer licenses are resident-only until the leftover period, and the East River Special Buck is resident-only. Nonresident archery deer for public and private land (ADNP-ST1) is a draw (2,200 licenses in 2026); preference points are $20 for nonresidents. Nonresident quotas are printed per unit in each season's application (e.g. 2026 West River unit 02A type 01: 400 resident, 32 nonresident).
species.otcSummary: Resident archery deer licenses (ST1, ER1, WR1, LM1) are unlimited and sold over the counter from 2026-06-10; nonresident private-land-only archery buck (ADN-ST1) and antlerless whitetail archery (ADNP-LM1) licenses are unlimited over the counter; muzzleloader antlerless whitetail (LM1-13) is unlimited over the counter from 2026-09-03; leftover rifle licenses are first-come, first-served after the fourth draw.

species.drawSystemSummary: Firearms antelope (prairie units), Custer State Park antelope, Special Antelope (private land) and nonresident archery antelope are drawn with the same preference pools as deer: landowners with preference (50%), then 2+, 1+ and 0+ preference pools and second choices, with GFP cubing each applicant's entries.
species.residentNote: Unsuccessful first-choice applicants may buy a preference point ($5). Successful Custer State Park antelope applicants cannot reapply for nine years. Two firearms draws in 2026.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents may apply for prairie firearms units (small nonresident quotas, e.g. 2026 unit 27A: 350 resident / 7 nonresident), Special Antelope (2026: 50 resident / 50 nonresident) and the nonresident archery public & private land draw; CSP antelope is resident-only. Preference points $20.
species.otcSummary: GFP's draw statistics include no resident archery antelope drawing; GFP Key Dates lists the archery antelope application/purchase window as Jul 22 - Oct 31, 2026. Eligible nonresident landowners may buy a landowner-own-land firearm antelope license.

species.drawSystemSummary: Ram-only bighorn licenses for the Black Hills (BHS, units BH2 and BH4) and Custer State Park (CBS, CU1) are drawn for residents; GFP's draw results show 10+, 2+ and 0+ preference pools, and every bighorn season and unit is once in a lifetime.
species.residentNote: Only South Dakota residents who have never received a South Dakota bighorn sheep license may apply; unsuccessful applicants receive a preference point automatically; no group applications; $10 non-refundable application fee; successful hunters must attend an orientation. 2026 quotas: BH2 3, BH4 2, CU1 2.

species.drawSystemSummary: GFP lists the mountain goat hunting season as closed. The last mountain goat drawing in GFP's draw statistics is 2022 (license BG155, one any mountain goat, Black Hills), shown here as history only.

Resident mountain lion licenses ($30) are unlimited and sold over the counter; the Black Hills Fire Protection District season closes early when 60 lions or 40 females are taken. Access permits to hunt with dogs in a designated part of the Black Hills Fire Protection District are issued by random drawing for set hunting intervals (3 permits per interval in 2026); GFP's draw statistics title this drawing 'Custer State Park Mountain Lion Access Permit' for 2023-2025 and 'Mountain Lion Access Permit' for 2026.
species.residentNote: One mountain lion per person per season; access permit required only to hunt with dogs inside the designated Black Hills area.
species.nonresidentNote: No nonresident mountain lion license (GFP fee table lists N/A).
species.otcSummary: Resident license over the counter, unlimited: 2026 season purchases opened 2025-11-26.

species.drawSystemSummary: Prairie spring and prairie fall turkey licenses, nonresident Black Hills spring, Custer State Park spring and archery access permits are drawn with GFP's landowner and 2+/1+/0+ preference pools (cubed entries); in the third prairie spring draw remaining licenses are pooled for residents and nonresidents.
species.residentNote: Residents may apply for all prairie units; Black Hills spring (BST) and archery (AST) licenses are unlimited over the counter for residents; Custer State Park spring (100 licenses in 2026) and archery access permits are resident-only draws.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents may apply for prairie units west of the Missouri River and East River licenses remaining after the second drawing; the nonresident Black Hills spring license is a limited draw (2,225 licenses in 2026); archery turkey is unlimited for nonresidents.
species.otcSummary: Spring archery (statewide except CSP), resident Black Hills spring and mentored licenses over the counter; leftover prairie licenses first-come, first-served.
